question: How did Mary's life end: death, or assumption?

answers.label: Scripture does not say, and no one knows
She died (fell asleep) and was taken up by her Son
She was assumed body and soul into heaven

overview.text: Epiphanius, about 377, the first to discuss it, says Scripture is silent and no one knows whether she died or was buried.
From the fifth century, stories of her "passing" (Transitus) spread, and by about 600 the Dormition was a feast across the empire. The Orthodox and Copts sing of her death and of her body taken up.
In 1950 Pius XII defined the Assumption, body and soul, without deciding whether she died first.

quotes.author: Epiphanius of Salamis
quotes.english: Let them search the traces of the Scriptures, and they will find neither Mary's death, nor whether she died or did not die, nor whether she was buried or not buried ... For I do not dare to say it; I keep silent in thought. ... I do not say that she remained immortal, nor do I affirm that she died. For Scripture went beyond the human mind and left it in suspense, because of that honored and outstanding vessel. ... If she died, we do not know.
quotes.original: ζητήσωσι τὰ ἴχνη τῶν γραφῶν καὶ εὕρωσιν ἂν οὔτε θάνατον Μαρίας οὔτε εἰ τέθνηκεν οὔτε εἰ μὴ τέθνηκεν, οὔτε εἰ τέθαπται οὔτε εἰ μὴ τέθαπται ... ἐγὼ γὰρ οὐ τολμῶ λέγειν, ἀλλὰ διανοούμενος σιωπὴν ἀσκῶ ... καὶ οὐ λέγω ὅτι ἀθάνατος ἔμεινεν· ἀλλ' οὔτε διαβεβαιοῦμαι εἰ τέθνηκεν. ὑπερέβαλε γὰρ ἡ γραφὴ τὸν νοῦν τὸν ἀνθρώπινον καὶ ἐν μετεώρῳ εἴασε διὰ τὸ σκεῦος τὸ τίμιον καὶ ἐξοχώτατον ... κἄν τε οὖν τέθνηκεν, οὐκ ἔγνωμεν
quotes.context: The earliest Christian writer to address the question, about 377, a bishop from Palestine. He knew no tradition of her death or her tomb.

quotes.author: Transitus Mariae
quotes.english: And the Lord, stretching out his undefiled hands, received her holy and blameless soul
quotes.original: τοῦ κυρίου ἁπλώσαντος τὰς ἀχράντους αὐτοῦ χεῖρας ἐδέξατο τὴν ἁγίαν καὶ ἄμωμον αὐτῆς ψυχήν
quotes.context: A legend of about the fifth century, the narrative root of the Dormition feast. It is the earliest surviving telling of Mary's end, not a historical record; in it the apostles are gathered to her and the Lord himself receives her soul.

quotes.author: Gregory of Tours
quotes.work: On the Glory of the Martyrs
quotes.english: At last, when the blessed Mary had completed the course of this life and was now being called from the world, all the apostles gathered from their several regions to her house. ... and behold, the Lord Jesus came with his angels, and receiving her soul, he handed it to Michael the archangel, and departed. ... And behold, the Lord stood by them again, and ordered the holy body he had taken up to be carried on a cloud into paradise: where now, her soul restored to her, she rejoices with his chosen ones and enjoys the good things of eternity, which will never come to an end.
quotes.original: Denique impleto a beata Maria hujus vitæ cursu, cum jam vocaretur a sæculo, congregati sunt omnes apostoli de singulis regionibus ad domum ejus. ... et ecce Dominus Jesus advenit cum angelis suis, et accipiens animam ejus, tradidit Michaeli archangelo, et recessit. ... Et ecce iterum adstitit eis Dominus, susceptumque corpus sanctum in nube deferri jussit in paradisum: ubi nunc, resumpta anima, cum electis ejus exsultans, æternitatis bonis, nullo occasuris fine, perfruitur.
quotes.context: The first Latin telling of her end. Gregory, bishop of Tours in Gaul, retells the Transitus story a century and a half after it began to circulate in the East: her soul is received by her Son, her body waits in the tomb, and then it too is carried to paradise. He is read here in Bordier's edition (Paris, 1857), the text of Ruinart collated on new manuscripts. Krusch's MGH edition has the same chapter division, but no open scan of it could be lawfully reached.

quotes.author: Orthodox Church
quotes.english: Neither the tomb, nor death had power over the Theotokos
quotes.original: Neither the tomb, nor death had power over the Theotokos
quotes.context: The feast of the Dormition ("falling asleep") on 15 August was fixed for the whole empire by Emperor Maurice about 600. The kontakion is sung in the Orthodox liturgy.

source.edition: Kontakion of the Dormition (Orthodox Church in America)

quotes.author: John of Damascus
quotes.locus: Homily 2.18 — Juvenal and the empty tomb
quotes.english: The facts of the end of the holy Mother of God Mary are not recorded in holy and God-inspired Scripture; but we have received from an ancient and most truthful tradition what took place at the time of her glorious falling asleep. ... Her all-hymned body they could not find at all; they found only her grave-cloths lying there. ... He himself was pleased, after her departure from this life, to honour her undefiled and unstained body with incorruption, and with a translation before the common and universal resurrection.
quotes.original: Τῇ μὲν ἁγίᾳ καὶ θεοπνεύστῳ Γραφῇ οὐκ ἐμφέρεται τὰ κατὰ τὴν τελευτὴν τῆς ἁγίας Θεοτόκου Μαρίας· ἐξ ἀρχαίας δὲ καὶ ἀληθεστάτης παραδόσεως παρειλήφαμεν, ὅτι ἐν τῷ καιρῷ τῆς ἐνδόξου κοιμήσεως αὐτῆς ... Καὶ τὸ μὲν σῶμα αὐτῆς τὸ πανύμνητον οὐδαμῶς εὑρεῖν ἠδυνήθησαν, μόνα δὲ αὐτῆς τὰ ἐντάφια κείμενα εὑρόντες ... αὐτὸς εὐδόκησε καὶ μετὰ τὴν ἐντεῦθεν ἀποβίωσιν, τὸ ταύτης ἄχραντον καὶ ἀμίαντον σῶμα τῇ ἀφθαρσίᾳ τιμῆσαι, καὶ μεταθέσει πρὸ τῆς κοινῆς καὶ καθολικῆς ἀναστάσεως
quotes.context: Preaching on the feast, John quotes the lost Euthymius History (book 3, ch. 40) word for word. The emperor Marcian and Pulcheria had asked Juvenal, Jerusalem's archbishop, to send Mary's body to Constantinople as the new capital's protection. Juvenal's answer is why there were no relics to send: the apostles had opened her tomb for Thomas and found it empty. John's Greek was read in Migne's PG 96 (Paris, 1860), openly posted on archive.org; an earlier pass wrongly recorded that no PG 96 text is openly posted.

quotes.author: Coptic Orthodox Church (Pope Shenouda III)
quotes.english: The Church believes in the Ascent of the body of The Virgin to heaven, and celebrates that feast on the 16th of Misra.
quotes.original: The Church believes in the Ascent of the body of The Virgin to heaven, and celebrates that feast on the 16th of Misra.
quotes.context: The Copts keep both her death (21 Tobah) and the bodily ascent (16 Misra).

source.edition: Pope Shenouda III (Coptic Orthodox), The Holy Virgin Saint Mary

quotes.author: Pius XII
quotes.english: that the Immaculate Mother of God, the ever Virgin Mary, having completed the course of her earthly life, was assumed body and soul into heavenly glory.
quotes.original: that the Immaculate Mother of God, the ever Virgin Mary, having completed the course of her earthly life, was assumed body and soul into heavenly glory.
quotes.context: Defined in 1950. The definition does not say whether Mary died first.

method: Every early quote was read in its Greek or Latin and translated for this page by Claude (Opus 5.5) on 13 October 2026. Each line names the printed edition it was read from.
